name: Can my old bathtub really be replaced with a walk-in shower without making the bathroom worse?

mainEntity.name: Can my old bathtub really be replaced with a walk-in shower without making the bathroom worse?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, a tub-to-walk-in-shower conversion can improve access, but the best layout depends on the bathroom’s size, drain location, door swing, and how much floor slope is available. Elite Remodeling & Design can evaluate the existing bathroom during consultation and coordinate design, plumbing, construction, and inspection planning.

A low-threshold shower is not automatically barrier-free. The finished entry, shower pan, drain, waterproofing, controls, and surrounding floor all affect usability.

Key factors:
- Existing drain and supply-line locations
- Threshold height and available floor depth
- Door, glass, bench, and grab-bar placement
- Wall and subfloor conditions after demolition

Before requesting a proposal, measure the room, photograph the current tub and plumbing wall, and list mobility concerns. Ask how the proposed pan will be waterproofed and tested before tile is installed.

A coordinated design-build process can help keep accessibility goals aligned with construction realities.
acceptedAnswer.description: Usually, yes—but the result depends on the drain, floor depth, threshold, door clearance, and wall conditions. Have the existing bathroom assessed before choosing fixtures. A proper plan should address the shower pan, waterproofing, controls, glass, and any bench or grab bars together.
